title: Archive Spell 1: Creating and reading profile cards
lessonSummary: Great! You create dictionaries and read values by their key.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: create a dictionary and read from it.
Create a dictionary hero with the keys name ("Aria"), class ("Mage"), level (15) and hp (120). Print exactly Name: Aria and on the next line Level: 15 (access with []).
The dictionary hero is given. Print the number of entries with len() as Number of properties: 4 and on the next line Class: Mage.

title: Archive Spell 2: Changing, adding and removing
lessonSummary: Nice! You change values, add entries and remove them again.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: change, add, remove.
tasks.codeTemplate:
hero = {"name": "Aria", "class": "Mage", "level": 15, "hp": 120}
hero["level"] = hero["level"] + 1
hero["mana"] = 80
removed = hero.pop("hp")
print(f"Level now: {hero['level']}")
print(f"Removed: {removed}")
print(f"Properties: {len(hero)}")

tasks.instruction: The dictionary hero is given. Increase level with += 1 and add the new key mana with the value 80. Print exactly Level: 16 and on the next line Mana: 80.
The dictionary hero is given. Remove the key class with pop() and print the removed value as Removed: Mage. Then delete the key hp with del and print Properties: 2 (len).

title: Archive Spell 3: Safe access with get() and in
lessonSummary: Well done! You ask with get() and in instead of risking a KeyError.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: get() with a default value and in.
tasks.codeTemplate:
hero = {"name": "Aria", "class": "Mage", "level": 15, "hp": 120}
print("Name:", hero.get("name"))
print("Mana:", hero.get("mana", 0))
print("Present:", "mana" in hero)

tasks.instruction: The dictionary hero is given (without mana). Fetch the value of mana with get() and default value 0 and print exactly Mana: 0.
The dictionary hero is given. Check with in and print exactly level present: True and on the next line mana present: False.

validation.expected:
level present: True
mana present: False

title: Archive Spell 4: Looping through dictionaries
lessonSummary: Great! You walk through a dictionary with keys(), values() and items().

tasks.instruction: Run this example: items() and values().
The dictionary bag is given (Bag: name and amount). With items(), print each entry as Name: Amount on its own line, e.g. Potion: 3.
The dictionary bag is given. Add up all amounts with values() and print exactly Total: 10 and on the next line Kinds: 3 (len).

title: Archive Spell 5: Tuples
lessonSummary: Nice! You pack values into tuples and unpack them again.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: create, read and unpack a tuple.
tasks.codeTemplate:
artifact = ("Fire staff", 15, "Fire")
print(artifact)
print("Length:", len(artifact))
print("First:", artifact[0])
name, value, kind = artifact
print(f"Value: {value}")

tasks.instruction: Create the tuple artifact = ("Fire staff", 15, "Fire") and unpack it into name, value and kind. Print exactly Name: Fire staff and on the next line Kind: Fire.
Two points are given as tuples. Calculate the distance as the difference of the x values plus the difference of the y values (goal minus start, all positive) and print exactly Distance: 7.

title: Archive Spell 6: Immutable and catching errors
lessonSummary: Masterful! You catch errors with try/except instead of letting your program crash.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: catch three kinds of errors.
The tuple artifact is given. In a try block, try to set artifact[1] = 99, catch the TypeError and print exactly Error: protected.
The dictionary bag is given. In a try block, try to read bag["Dragon egg"], catch the KeyError and print exactly Not in store: Dragon egg.
The input text = "ten" is given. In a try block, convert it to number with int(). Catch the ValueError and then set number = 0. Print exactly Number: 0.

title: Archive Spell 7: Nested structures
lessonSummary: World class! You nest dictionaries, lists and tuples.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: read nested data and filter.
tasks.codeTemplate:
hero = {"name": "Aria", "class": "Mage", "level": 15, "hp": 120, "equipment": {"weapon": "Staff", "armor": "Robe"}}
print(f"Weapon: {hero['equipment']['weapon']}")
heroes = [
    {"name": "Aria", "class": "Mage", "level": 15, "hp": 120},
    {"name": "Thorin", "class": "Warrior", "level": 18, "hp": 150},
    {"name": "Luna", "class": "Rogue", "level": 12, "hp": 90},
]
print(f"Count: {len(heroes)}")
strong = [e["name"] for e in heroes if e["level"] > 14]
print(f"Strong: {strong}")

tasks.instruction: The list heroes with three dictionaries is given. Print exactly Count: 3 and on the next line Last: Luna (name of the last entry, index -1).
The dictionary hero contains the sub-entry equipment and is given. Print exactly Weapon: Staff and on the next line Armor: Robe.
The list heroes is given. With a list comprehension, collect the names of all entries whose level is greater than 14 into strong and print exactly Strong: ['Aria', 'Thorin'].

title: Debug Quest
lessonSummary: All bugs found! With dictionaries and tuples, commas, keys and immutability matter.

title: Mission 3: The Hero Guild
lessonSummary: Mission accomplished: Searching, counting and averaging across a whole list of profile cards!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Loop: The list heroes with four dictionaries is given. Print each entry as Name: Level on its own line, e.g. Aria: 15.

title: Extra Challenge 2: The Dungeon Manager
lessonSummary: The manager runs: nested dictionaries searched, compared and evaluated!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Setup: The nested dictionary zones is given (Level → dictionary with monster, treasure, difficulty). Print each Level as Name: monster / treasure, e.g. Cellar: Rat / Silver.

validation.expected:
Cellar: Rat / Silver
Cave: Troll / Gold
Tower: Dragon / Crown

tasks.instruction: Step 2 – Most dangerous: The dictionary zones is given. Find the Level with the highest difficulty and print exactly Most dangerous: Tower (8).
Step 3 – Who may enter? The character has strong = 5. In the list enterable, collect the names of all zones whose difficulty is at most strong and print exactly Enterable: ['Cellar', 'Cave'].

title: Extra Challenge 3: The Hero Archive
lessonSummary: The archive stands: searching, counting and a ranking from four profile cards!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Create: Create the list heroes with four dictionaries (keys name, class, level): Aria (Mage, 15), Thorin (Warrior, 18), Luna (Rogue, 12), Mira (Mage, 13). Print exactly Count: 4.
Step 2 – Search: The list heroes is given. Write a function find_heroes(items, kind) that returns the names with this class. Print exactly Mage: 2 and on the next line Warrior: 1 (number of hits).

Step 3 – Ranking: The list heroes is given. Collect all level values, sort them in descending order and find the name with the highest value. Print exactly Best: Thorin and on the next line Ranking: [18, 15, 13, 12].

title: Extra Challenge 4: The Great Guild Archive
lessonSummary: The great review is done: functions, lists and randomness from weeks 5 to 7 – now with dictionaries!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Function with return (week 5): Write create_hero(name, kind, level) that returns a dictionary with the keys name, class, level. Call it with ("Aria", "Mage", 15) and print exactly Created: Aria and on the next line Level: 15.

Step 2 – List of dictionaries (week 5/6): Write create_quest(name, difficulty) that returns a dictionary with name, difficulty and status "open". Create the list quests and add three Quest entries with append() (Defeat the dragon / 1, Find the treasure / 2, Save the village / 3). Print exactly Quest count: 3 and on the next line Status: open (status of the first one).
Step 3 – Find the largest value (week 6): The dictionary prices (name → price) is given. Find the most expensive item with a loop and print exactly Most expensive item: Potion (30).
Step 4 – Counting with a dictionary: In word = "adventure", count how often each letter occurs. Use counter = {} and counter[c] = counter.get(c, 0) + 1. Print exactly e: 2.
Step 5 – Randomness (week 7): The dictionary bag is given. With random.choice(list(bag.keys())), draw a name into drawn and print exactly Drawn valid: True (drawn in bag).

Step 6 – Catch errors (week 5/8): The dictionary bag is given. Write amount_of(name) that returns the amount – or 0 if the name is missing (try/except KeyError). Print exactly Potion: 3 and on the next line Dragon egg: 0.
